program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-entry deep passes; consolidate and validate once after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Public PubMed/PMC web records used when NCBI EFetch returned HTTP 429
source-specific manual claim-direction, population, formulation, route, and safety calibration

policy.validation_strategy: deep source calibration per pass; expensive repository-wide validation after Wave 2500

waves.title: Efficacy and safety of Buyang Huanwu Decoction combined with α-lipoic acid for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a systematic review with in-depth heterogeneity deconstruction and methodological appraisal.
waves.finding: Buyang Huanwu Decoction plus alpha-lipoic acid improved subjective response and symptom scores versus comparator regimens, but nerve-conduction outcomes were extremely heterogeneous and reliable quantitative conclusions were not possible.
waves.safety: Combination therapy prevents attribution to alpha-lipoic acid alone; adverse-event rates did not differ clearly.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotic and Synbiotic Supplementation on Glycemic Indices in Adult Individuals with Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Grade-Assessed Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-analysis of RCTs.
waves.population: adults with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes
waves.finding: Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation modestly reduced fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HbA1c, and HOMA-IR, with substantial heterogeneity across outcomes.
waves.safety: Effects are strain- and formulation-dependent; duration meta-regression did not establish a simple dose-time rule.

waves.title: Comparative effectiveness and safety of probiotics with psychotropic potential in mental health benefits in irritable bowel syndrome: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
waves.population: 3,154 participants with IBS across nine treatment nodes
waves.finding: Some probiotic strains or combinations ranked better than placebo for quality of life, depression, or anxiety, but effects differed markedly by strain and outcome.
waves.safety: Network rankings should not be generalized to all probiotics; direct head-to-head evidence was limited.

waves.title: Efficacy of probiotic supplementation for body weight management in overweight and obese adults: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials predominantly from East Asia.
waves.population: adults with overweight or obesity, predominantly East Asian studies
waves.finding: Probiotics produced small reductions in weight, BMI, waist circumference, and body-fat percentage but did not significantly improve total cholesterol or triglycerides.
waves.safety: Strain specificity, regional concentration, and co-interventions such as health guidance limit broad recommendations.

waves.title: Effectiveness of probiotic supplementation in managing depressive symptoms and inflammatory status in patients with depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review with 7 studies in meta-analysis
waves.finding: Probiotic supplementation was associated with improvement in depressive symptoms but did not significantly change IL-6 or TNF-alpha.
waves.safety: The clinical significance and strain-specificity remain uncertain; probiotics should be interpreted as adjunctive evidence.

waves.title: The Complementary and Alternative Roles of Curcumin in Treatment of Ulcerative Colitis: An Umbrella Review.
waves.finding: Many pooled curcumin outcomes were statistically significant, but none were supported by high-certainty evidence and methodological weaknesses were widespread.
waves.safety: Evidence remains uncertain despite positive pooled signals; formulation and adjunctive-treatment differences matter.

waves.title: N-acetylcysteine nano-spray versus conventional treatment in the management of radiotherapy-induced oral mucositis in oral cancer patients: a randomized clinical trial.
waves.finding: A NAC nano-spray reduced oral-mucositis severity and improved oral-health-related quality of life versus conventional therapy during a six-week radiotherapy course.
waves.safety: Very small study and nano-spray route/formulation prevent extrapolation to oral NAC supplements.

waves.title: Correlations between iodine status and the risk of thyroid nodules, a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Iodine status showed a U-shaped association with thyroid-nodule prevalence, with higher risk at deficient and very high urinary iodine levels; evidence certainty was low and heterogeneity substantial.
waves.safety: Cross-sectional urinary-iodine associations cannot establish that iodine supplementation causes or prevents nodules.

waves.title: Effects of astaxanthin supplementation on human sperm quality during the freeze thaw process: a systematic review and meta analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of sperm cryopreservation studies
waves.population: human sperm evaluated during freeze-thaw processing
waves.finding: Astaxanthin improved post-thaw viability, morphology, progressive motility, and selected kinematic measures but did not significantly improve total motility or DNA damage.
waves.safety: This is largely ex-vivo cryopreservation evidence and does not establish benefits from oral astaxanthin supplementation in men.

waves.title: Vitamin D and Bisphosphonate Therapy for Optimizing Outcomes in Spinal Fusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized and prospective comparative trials
waves.finding: Perioperative vitamin D was associated with improved one-year fusion and disability outcomes versus placebo/no supplement; bisphosphonates accelerated early fusion and reduced vertebral-fracture risk, with convergence of fusion outcomes by one year.
waves.safety: Highly clinical perioperative context and comparisons with bisphosphonates limit general supplement interpretation.

waves.title: High versus standard dose folic acid supplementation for miscarriage prevention: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: 5,144 women trying to conceive; 1,488 pregnancies in primary miscarriage analysis
waves.finding: Preconception high-dose folic acid was associated with lower miscarriage risk among women who became pregnant and a higher pregnancy rate, but the intention-to-treat miscarriage analysis was not statistically significant.
waves.safety: Evidence certainty was low-to-moderate and the studied high dose (4-5 mg/day) is far above standard OTC prevention dosing; no consumer dose recommendation is justified.

waves.title: Effects of the Edible Microalga Chlorella on Gut Microbiota and on Brain Health: Current Evidence and Emerging Links.
waves.population: 21 included studies; predominantly animal models with few human trials
waves.finding: Most studies reported favorable gut-microbiota or neurobehavioral signals, but the evidence base was predominantly preclinical and rarely measured gut and brain outcomes together.
waves.safety: Human efficacy is not established; mechanistic and animal signals should remain clearly separated from clinical claims.

waves.title: Zinc-based therapies for prevention and treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis including observational and interventional studies
waves.finding: Systemic zinc levels were lower in women with vulvovaginal candidiasis, but supplementation did not significantly reduce 90-day reinfection in the small RCT and routine zinc-based therapy was not supported.
waves.safety: Lower zinc may reflect host nutritional immunity rather than deficiency; causal supplementation claims are not established.

waves.title: Ginseng Bioactive Components as Gut-Brain Axis-Targeted Modulators: Therapeutic Potential and Mechanisms in Multifactorial Diseases.
waves.finding: Ginseng components were linked to gut-microbiota, barrier, inflammatory, and neurotransmitter pathways across multiple disease models, but most supporting evidence was preclinical.
waves.safety: Clinical efficacy via the gut-brain axis remains unproven and requires human trials.

waves.title: Enhanced Bioavailability of a Novel Oil-Based Lutein Formulation: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Single-Dose, Comparative Oral Bioavailability Study in Healthy Adults.
waves.study: randomized double-blind single-dose comparative bioavailability study
waves.finding: A novel oil-based lutein formulation produced higher serum Cmax and AUC than a reference lutein formulation after a single 25-mg fed dose.
waves.safety: Both formulations were well tolerated; this is formulation-specific pharmacokinetic evidence and does not demonstrate superior clinical outcomes.

waves.title: Efficacy and Safety of Salvia miltiorrhiza Extract (SAGX) Compared with Saw Palmetto in Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A 12-Week, Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group Pilot Study.
waves.population: 30 men with lower urinary tract symptoms
waves.finding: The proprietary Salvia extract improved IPSS, storage symptoms, quality of life, and erectile-function scores more than saw palmetto in this small pilot.
waves.safety: Adverse events were mild and transient, but the sample was very small and several authors were sponsor employees; product-specific evidence only.

waves.title: Efficacy and effectiveness of melatonin for the management of musculoskeletal pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo and active controlled trials.
waves.population: 2,028 people with chronic or postoperative musculoskeletal pain
waves.finding: Melatonin was not clearly superior to placebo for chronic musculoskeletal pain in the main analysis, showed modest benefits versus active controls and in sensitivity analyses, and most effects did not reach minimal clinically important thresholds.
waves.safety: Adverse events were generally mild and transient; evidence certainty was low-to-moderate and supports, at most, an adjunctive role.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotics on Markers of Oxidative/Nitrosative Stress and Damage Associated with Inflammation in Non-communicable Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trials.
waves.finding: Probiotics improved some antioxidant/oxidative-stress markers and hsCRP but not nitric oxide, 8-OHdG, IL-6, or TNF-alpha; heterogeneity was very high.
waves.safety: Strain and disease heterogeneity make category-wide clinical claims inappropriate.

waves.title: The effect of prenatal balanced energy and protein supplementation on small vulnerable newborn types in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis of individual participant data.
waves.population: 10,252 pregnancies in low- and middle-income countries
waves.finding: Prenatal balanced energy/protein supplementation reduced several combinations of preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age birth, and low birthweight, with effect magnitude varying by maternal factors and timing.
waves.safety: This is prenatal food/nutrition-intervention evidence, not generic protein-powder evidence.

waves.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids Supplementation Improves Pulmonary Function and Clinical Outcomes in Critically Ill Patients: a Meta-Analysis.
waves.finding: Omega-3 interventions improved several oxygenation and inflammatory measures and were associated with shorter ventilation and hospital duration.
waves.safety: Both enteral and parenteral routes were pooled; critical-care formulations and routes prevent extrapolation to routine consumer fish-oil use.

waves.title: Effects of probiotics on cognitive function across the human lifespan: a meta-analysis.
waves.population: participants across infant, child, young-adult, and older-adult age groups
waves.finding: Probiotic effects differed by age and cognitive domain, with pooled benefits most apparent in older adults for global cognition, processing speed, memory, and spatial ability.
waves.safety: The meta-analysis pooled diverse strains and suggested subgroup regimens; strain-specific replication is required before dosing claims.

waves.title: Caffeine makes a splash: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis exploring the effects of caffeine intake on swimming performance.
waves.study: systematic review/multilevel meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled crossover trials
waves.finding: Acute caffeine improved swimming performance by about 1.7% on average and increased post-test lactate, with substantial between-study heterogeneity.
waves.safety: Dose subgroup signals were exploratory and do not establish an optimal or universally safe dose.

waves.title: Effects of Curcumin/Turmeric Supplementation on Kidney Function in Individuals With Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
waves.finding: Curcumin/turmeric did not significantly change creatinine, BUN, uric acid, or albumin; urea decreased modestly, with moderate-to-low certainty depending on outcome.
waves.safety: This does not demonstrate a clinically meaningful renoprotective effect; publication bias was detected for creatinine.

waves.title: Efficacy and Safety of Probiotic Supplementation for Neonatal Jaundice: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Adjunctive probiotics reduced bilirubin over the first 10 days and shortened phototherapy and hospital duration; reported short-term adverse effects were lower.
waves.safety: Neonatal use is highly population- and strain-specific; sustained effects and routine implementation remain uncertain.

waves.title: Vitamin D supplementation for prevention of vitamin D deficiency in preterm and low birth weight infants.
waves.finding: Vitamin D supplementation reduced deficiency risk; higher doses reduced deficiency further but increased vitamin-D excess, while evidence for broader bone-health or morbidity outcomes remained limited or uncertain.
waves.safety: Higher-dose regimens increased vitamin-D excess risk; neonatal dosing requires clinical oversight and should not be generalized to healthy children or adults.
